title: $6,270,000 2025 U.S. Department of Education Office of Elementary and Secondary Education, Education and Innovation Research (EIR) Program Early-phase Grant (CFDA 84.411C) Priority 4 (competitive priorities 1 and 2). Mosher, M. (Principal), Dieker, L., Shomaji, S., Lane, K., & Bruce Frey (Co-Principals) The project team proposes using the innovation of artificial intelligence (AI) to create a progress monitoring (PM) platform to support teachers, students, and parents, Innovative Solutions for Personalized Instruction and Resilience in Education (InspirED-AI). The need for this platform in grades 4-8 is critical due to the disruption of support for adolescents post-COVID, leading to a doubling in severe internalizing mental health problems (Gotlib et al., 2023), altered social neurodevelopment (Racine et al., 2021), and decreased self-efficacy and emotion-regulation (Skinner et al., 2023). The team will build upon existing evidence-based practices (EBPs) and PM in social, emotional, and behavioral skills to create an AI platform to close the post-COVID gap for students at risk and those with disabilities. The team, partnered with five leading AI experts (AI Dev Lab) who are providing a 10% match for the 5.7 million dollar project, and will create an open-education resource AI Suite (free) to decrease teacher time spent PM, increase student understanding of their behavior, increase parent communication, and improve student outcomes (08/01/2025-07/31/2029).

group: Johns Hopkins University School of Engineering Adjunct Professor; Course Writer/Developer
title: EN.635.755†: Strategic Design and Development in Extended Reality (XR; Spring & Summer 2026). Designed the syllabus, rubrics, and technical labs focusing on Unity, C#, and AI integration for enterprise and educational applications. In this course, students learn about and explore Extended Reality (XR), encompassing Virtual and Augmented Reality (VR/AR), and its use as a catalyst for enterprise innovation and data-driven decision-making. Students evaluate the business case, technical requirements, and potential return on investment for XR and AI solutions. Through hands-on application, students develop interactive VR and AR prototypes using the Unity engine and C# programming language, implementing core mechanics such as physics-based interactions and spatial UI/UX design. Students research and analyze unique security vulnerabilities and ethical considerations inherent in immersive technologies and artificial intelligence. Through teacher-guided, hands-on instruction, students design a comprehensive project plan to manage the full product lifecycle from concept through deployment. Prerequisite: Core Coding. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: SPED 730†: Characteristics, Methods & Assessment: Introduction to Struggling Learners & Students with High-Incidence Disabilities (Fall 2021) Assisted in the redesign and teaching of SPED 730 a course designed as an introduction to the characteristics, assessment and identification process, and initial instructional and behavioral interventions needed in meeting the needs of students with high-incidence disabilities under the Kansas Adaptive Teacher Education Standards. The needs for specialized services to meet specific learning and/or behavioral needs are presented. Frameworks for instruction and conceptualizing best practice are introduced including the principles of Universal Design for Learning and the Multi-Tier System of Support. The role of the educator in identifying, understanding, and implementing evidence-based practices is examined. Curriculum resources and intervention strategies for students with high-incidence disabilities is introduced with emphasis on tiered planning and implementation. The course is intended for persons working toward the Kansas teaching endorsement in the Special Education Adaptive Area. Prerequisite: Admittance into the Adaptive endorsement teacher education program in the Department of Special Education or permission of the instructor. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: SPED 326: Teaching Exceptional Children and Youth in General Education (Fall 2021) Assisted in teaching SPED 326 a course designed for general education teacher trainees. It provides information about students with disabilities that they will have in their classrooms and the law governing special education and its implications for them as general educators. The course addresses Individualized Educational Plans that are developed for students with disabilities and how general educators contribute to these plans. Students learn about planning instruction that is differentiated to meet various learner needs, universal design principles, and instructional tools. Students are also provided with resources to help provide meaningful access to general education classrooms and curriculum for students with disabilities. Time is spent on designing and delivering appropriate accommodations and modifications to assist student learning. Prerequisite: Admission to the Teacher Education Program. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 715: Understanding Research in Education (Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the course designed to introduce the concepts and skills involved in understanding and analyzing research in education and related areas. The course provides an overview of basic, general knowledge of various quantitative and qualitative research methodologies. Emphasis is placed on enhancing students' ability to locate, read, comprehend, and critically analyze academic research articles and reports. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 720: Educational Measurement in the Classroom (Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the course designed to introduce the application of reliability, validity, and practicality concepts to the development, selection, use, and interpretation of tests and measuring instruments in education. The concepts of norm-referenced and criterion-referenced tests, the interpretation and use of norms, standard scores, and grading practices are covered. An understanding of the role of measurement in classroom evaluation, diagnosis, and placement is stressed. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 803: Computer Applications for Statistical Analyses (Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the course designed to teach the use of statistical computing software for data analysis and graphics in educational research. The course covers the creation and manipulation of data sets, alongside the execution of essential statistical procedures including descriptive statistics, t-tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA). Emphasis is placed on interpreting statistical results generated by computer packages and writing methods and results professionally. Prerequisite: EPSY 710 or EPSY 711. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 903: Computer Applications for Statistical Analyses (Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the course designed to explore advanced statistical software applications and programming for complex data analysis. Emphasis is placed on managing large-scale datasets, writing advanced syntax, and executing complex multivariate procedures such as structural equation modeling or hierarchical linear modeling. Students are required to interpret advanced statistical outputs and format results for scholarly publication. Prerequisite: EPSY 810 or EPSY 811. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 896: Research, Evaluation, Measurement, and Statistics Pro-Seminar (Spring & Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the REMS Proseminar, which is a community of scholars interested in research methods appropriate to Education and the Social Sciences. Each week, a guest speaker presents a topic they feel appeals to participants in research methods. It is available as a repeatable course for graduate students and as a learning community for faculty and staff to attend. 1 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 822: Educational Scales, Question Development, and Sampling (Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the course designed to learn about the development, construction, validation, and scaling of noncognitive instruments including questionnaires, surveys, checklists, rating scales and unobtrusive measures. The sampling methodology is emphasized. Item construction and analysis and the development of subscales are stressed. Prerequisite: EPSY 720 or EPSY 725 and EPSY 710. 3 Credit Course.

group: University of Kansas Professor; Course Developer; Guest Lecturer; Teaching Assistant
title: EPSY 902: Research, Evaluation, Measurement, and Statistics Pro-Seminar (Fall 2024) Guest lecturer for the course designed to examine the problems and procedures which relate to the validity of research methods. Emphasis is placed on reading the current literature on research methodology. Students are required to develop a research proposal. Prerequisite: EPSY 811 and EPSY 720 or EPSY 725. 3 Credit Course.

group: Baker University Adjunct Professor; Course Writer and Developer
title: SPED 707‡†: Multisensory Instructional Methods of Reading and Language Arts (Fall, Spring, and Summer Sessions, 2014-2022) Designed and taught Methods of Reading/Language Arts: K-6/5-8 (required for K-6 and 5-8 licensure) course. In this course, students screen, assess, and identify the needs of learners with high incidence disabilities in the areas of reading and language arts and intervene effectively using research and evidence-based strategies and methodologies. Prerequisite: SPED 700 Introduction and Characteristics of Students with High Incidence Disabilities. 3 Credit Course.

group: Baker University Adjunct Professor; Course Writer and Developer
title: EDU 5323†: Technology as Intervention (Fall, Spring, and Summer Sessions, 2013-2023) Proposed, designed, and taught this course in which students learn about and explore various forms of assistive technology, align assignments to the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework, discover techniques for differentiating instruction, practice implementing lessons in both a blended learning, hybrid and flipped classroom, and converse about educational technology trends and how these trends influence learning. Students are given the tools to determine the role of technology and when to and not to use technology to assist in providing various interventions. Through teacher-guided, learner-centered instruction, students learn to integrate technology into instruction based on a learner's needs. Students research the various levels of assistive technology and use their learning to create lesson plans and work collaboratively in projects. 3 Credit Course.

group: Baker University Adjunct Professor; Course Writer and Developer
title: SPED 705‡†: Educating Students with Social and Behavioral Needs (Fall and Spring Sessions, 2013-2016) Taught SPED 705 in which students learn to identify specific behavioral and social characteristics of learners with high incidence disabilities and the effect of trauma and tragedy on the student's ability to learn. Behavior intervention plans and functional behavioral assessments are presented along with a number of tiered models of support (i.e., Ci3T, PBIS). Students also gain knowledge of significant ways to use effective strategies and assessments to increase student success. Prerequisite: SPED 700 Introduction and Characteristics of Students with High Incidence Disabilities. 3 Credit Course.
